## jpegxl-rs.decision.c26-alias-mapping

### Revision 1 — C.2.6 alias mapping is symbols[u] = o, not 0

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.decision.c26-alias-mapping/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-entropy/**"` · topic `c26-alias-mapping`

In the C.2.6 alias-table build, symbols[u] = o (the overfull index), not 0. The
LaTeX renders it as 0, an OCR corruption; only o is consistent with the algorithm.
The invariant test (each symbol s appears exactly D[s] times across slots, offsets
a permutation of 0..D[s]) fails under = 0. If that test fires, the bug is in new
code, not the test.

**Context.** Recovered from HANDOFF "Already fixed" (2026-08-02).

## jpegxl-rs.decision.cover-rate-model-calibrated-for-target-rate

### Revision 1 — Target-rate requests price the cover objective's rate with the Phase Q4 calibrated model; fixed-quantizer defaults keep the legacy proxy

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.decision.cover-rate-model-calibrated-for-target-rate/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/src/lib.rs"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/src/request.rs"` · topic `cover-rate-model`

EncodeRequest::for_target sets cover_rate_model = CoverRateModel::Calibrated: a candidate's residual-bit proxy is scaled by 1.56 / 1.63 / 1.88 for DCT8x8 / DCT16x16 / DCT32x32 and each varblock is charged 5.5 / 12.4 / 10.5 fixed bits (non_zeros symbols plus a few bits of DctSelect signalling for merged blocks), replacing 1.0 / 1.0 / 1.0 and 2 / 34 / 34. block_cost_bounded scales its pruning arithmetic by the same factor, so CoverRateModel::Legacy is bit-identical to the Phase Q3 objective and remains the fixed-quantizer default and an explicit --cover-rate-model legacy control.

**Context.** tests/rate_proxy_audit.rs priced the chosen plan's I.4 events under the plan's own trained histograms on the three standing photos at 1 bpp Balanced: interior zeros cost 0.4-1.1 bits, nonzero tokens 3.3-4.1 bits, the three non_zeros symbols 5-11 bits per varblock, DctSelect signalling a few bits; the legacy proxy under-priced DCT8x8/16x16/32x32 residuals by 1.56x/1.63x/1.88x (mid), 1.52/1.58/1.76 (large), 1.84/1.89/2.0 (mid2), so it over-charged merging by its 32-bit constant and under-charged large transforms per coefficient.

**Consequences.** Against Phase Q3 the photo ladder moves SSIMULACRA2 +0.048 (worst -0.19), Butteraugli 3-norm -0.15%, max-norm mean +0.04%; the scenes +0.059 / -0.13% / +0.61%; timing neutral; Fast cells unchanged (fixed cover). The cover mix on the mid photo shifts from 42/38/20% DCT8/16/32 area to 33/52/16%. Phase 7.2's lambda_scale 4 was tuned against the legacy proxy; the absolute 1.56x scale therefore also lowers the cover's effective lambda, and a size-ordering-only variant (1.0/1.045/1.2) was worse on Butteraugli max-norm, so the absolute constants are the promoted ones.

## jpegxl-rs.decision.image-io-at-cli-boundary

### Revision 2 — Common raster format dependencies stay at the CLI boundary

`active` · `@jpegxl-rs.decision.image-io-at-cli-boundary/2` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/**"`

The high-level jpxl library facade remains pixel-buffer based and dependency-light. Common raster file decoding and encoding is an adapter concern of jpxl-cli, where the Rust image crate may be used without entering the normative decoder, encoder, or policy crates.

**Context.** General-use file conversion needs maintained PNG, JPEG, WebP, TIFF, BMP, QOI, TGA, and PNM implementations, while the project keeps normative codec crates near-zero-dependency.

**Consequences.** Library consumers pass ordinary interleaved 8/16-bit buffers without paying for unrelated file codecs. The CLI gains external image-format dependencies and owns their security/version maintenance.

**supersedes** `@jpegxl-rs.decision.image-io-at-cli-boundary/1`

## jpegxl-rs.decision.lossy-production-presets

### Revision 1 — Balanced and Fast are the production lossy presets; Quality is the exhaustive reference preset

`superseded` · `@jpegxl-rs.decision.lossy-production-presets/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-cli/src/main.rs"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/**"`, `path "JPXL/docs/optimize.md"`

Treat RateSearchPreset::Balanced and RateSearchPreset::Fast as the production-intended lossy paths. RateSearchPreset::Quality remains an exhaustive reference/oracle path for comparison, fallback, and research; it is not the primary target for production quality, latency, or efficiency work. New quality passes should first seek bounded, measured improvements to Balanced and Fast without silently routing their normal operation through Quality-tier work.

**Context.** The user clarified this preset contract on 2026-08-19 after Phase Q8 had improved only the Quality tier. Balanced and Fast already carry bounded two-anchor controllers and are the paths intended for real use; Quality deliberately pays exhaustive exact-search cost.

**Consequences.** Quality-only gains may still be recorded, but they do not satisfy a request to improve production encoding. Promotion reports must state which preset changes, prove unchanged presets stay byte-identical where claimed, and measure native Windows behavior when that is the faster available host path.

**superseded by** `@jpegxl-rs.decision.perceptual-quality-contract/1`

## jpegxl-rs.decision.modular-lean-default

### Revision 1 — Modular default effort is the lean level 1; the full search is opt-in

`active` · `@jpegxl-rs.decision.modular-lean-default/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-cli/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode/**"`

Effort::DEFAULT for the lossless modular path is Effort::MIN (level 1): one predictor, no split search, no per-leaf refinement, no palette/squeeze trials, coarse sampling stride, collapsed tree. The full pre-ramp search is retained verbatim at level 7 -- a byte-identical density anchor pinned by the effort_7_budget_is_the_pre_ramp_search test -- and levels 8-9 add finer stride and deeper search for density chasing. Effort is expanded once at the plan_for stage boundary into a ModularSearchBudget (Encoder-plan1.md 12), never re-checked in a kernel.

**Context.** The full search was measured to be chaff on the photo corpus: byte-identical output to level 1 at ~16x the wall time (jpegxl-rs.assessment.modular-effort-lean-default). Quality is preserved unconditionally because every level is exact-lossless.

**Consequences.** Default encodes are 4.6-16.9x faster on photos with byte-identical output (verified: .agent/scratch/effort-ramp-2026-08-10/verify_default_flip.ps1). Flat/paletteable content encodes a few percent larger by default (measured 3.7% on a synthetic screenshot) unless a higher effort is selected. This default-output change is deliberate but validated only on a limited corpus; a broader real-world UI/line-art corpus should confirm the tradeoff before any method is deleted (as opposed to demoted).

## jpegxl-rs.decision.opt-p-wide-rayon-deps

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.decision.opt-p-wide-rayon-deps/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/**"` · topic `opt-p-wide-rayon-deps`

The encoder optimization track may depend on the `wide` (portable SIMD)
and `rayon` (work-stealing pool) crates. Both are optional Cargo features
named `simd` and `parallel`, enabled by default on jpxl-core (simd),

--no-default-features remain pure-scalar and std::thread-only. Contract A
holds across thread counts for section emission; SIMD kernels may use
Contract B float semantics relative to scalar builds and stay decode-valid.

**Context.** Approved during Opt-P leaf-SIMD work after coarse section parallelism landed.

## jpegxl-rs.decision.optimization-determinism-contract

### Revision 1 — Contract A for structural optimization; bounded Contract B for quality policy

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.decision.optimization-determinism-contract/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-bitstream/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-entropy/**"`

Default to Contract A for optimization changes: same source and options produce identical codestream bytes across thread counts, scheduling, and scalar versus optimized integer/bitstream paths. Structural refactors (BitWriter bulk path, plan Arc-sharing, coefficient arenas, scratch reuse, Rayon section encoding, integer SIMD) must prove byte-identical output. Contract B permits deliberate quality-policy changes after a recorded corpus gate. Phase 5G's target-rate AQ/quant_lf gate required matched achieved rate, no Butteraugli regression in 12 representative cells, at least 7.5% observed Butteraugli improvement in every cell, RMSE improvement in every cell, and disclosed SSIMULACRA2 regression bounded to 4.5 points. Phase 5I's active-EPF gate separately requires matched achieved rate, no Butteraugli regression in 12 cells, at least 0.6% observed Butteraugli improvement in every cell, RMSE and Butteraugli-pnorm3 improvement in every cell, and any SSIMULACRA2 regression disclosed and bounded to 0.05 points. From the quality track (Phase Q0, 2026-08-17) onward, per jpegxl-rs.decision.ssimulacra2-is-the-primary-promotion-metric, a Contract B change (and any lossless-recoding change that moves target-rate outputs through the rate loop, such as Phase Q0b) is promoted only when, on the standing harness (.agent/scratch/quality-track: three photos x 0.5/1/2 bpp x Fast/Balanced/Quality plus the seven 1024x768 scenes at 1 bpp, candidate versus the previous promoted binary): SSIMULACRA2 mean delta >= 0 and no cell worse than -0.5; Butteraugli mean (max-norm) not worse than +2%; the worst-cell Butteraugli bound is stated on the 3-norm (butteraugli_pnorm3): no cell worse than +5% — the max-norm's single-cell value is reported but not bounded, because Phase Q1's sweeps measured it swinging +8% to +18% in single cells on settings whose SSIMULACRA2, RMSE and 3-norm were all neutral or better (a larger regression is a recorded trade, never an automatic promotion); bytes at matched SSIMULACRA2 not up; Balanced pinned wall within +15% cumulative of the Phase 42 binary (jpxl-p42d), instruction counts reported when the host is loaded; codestream bytes identical across 1 and 4 threads and with AVX2 disabled; djxl and jxl-oxide accept every stream. Future Contract B changes that need different bounds require another explicit revision naming them.

**Context.** VarDCT RD ties are sensitive to tiny float differences. Wide and hand SIMD can change NaN patterns and wrapping. The project already requires software-defined float conversion without fast-math for the reference pair. Phase 5G deliberately changed target-rate quantization policy. Phase 5I deliberately activates decoder restoration by signalling one EPF step and a uniform Sharpness 7 grid; this changes reconstructed pixels without changing coefficient decisions. The Phase 5G/5I bounds predate the SSIMULACRA2-first decision; the quality-track bounds restate the gate in its terms and add the speed budget and the third-party-decoder acceptance that Phase Q0b's jxl-oxide finding showed is not implied by djxl and jpxl-decode agreeing. Phase Q1 moved the worst-cell Butteraugli test to the 3-norm after measuring the max-norm's per-cell noise on the sweep.

**Consequences.** Every structural PR needs scalar-vs-optimized and 1-vs-N-thread byte equality tests where applicable. Float kernel and RD-search work may not claim Contract A without proof. Phase 5 target-rate quality policies may be promoted only while their recorded corpus evidence satisfies the separately stated Butteraugli, RMSE, achieved-rate, pnorm3, and SSIMULACRA2 bounds. Quality-track phases record their harness outputs (ladder/scenes/cjxl TSVs and summary) as evidence and state their speed cost against the +15% cumulative budget so later phases know what remains.

## jpegxl-rs.decision.optimization-ordering

### Revision 1 — Optimization order: structure, then parallel, then SIMD

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.decision.optimization-ordering/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-bitstream/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-core/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode/**"` · topic `optimization-ordering`

Within the encoder optimization pass, implement in this order: (1) separate
Modular and VarDCT benchmarks plus multiplicity counters; (2) remove repeated
full-frame work, deep plan clones, and per-varblock allocation; (3) replace
known-bad algorithms (bit-at-a-time writer, dense DCT32 fallback when factored
scalar exists, brute-force LZ only if hot); (4) reshape hot scalar loops for
the compiler; (5) coarse group and section parallelism with a single resource
policy; (6) explicit SIMD only on remaining leaf kernels; (7) LTO and PGO last.
Do not start with a general SIMD or Rayon sweep.

**Context.** Advisor static assessment. Aligns with correctness-before-speed (scalar before parallelism before SIMD).

## jpegxl-rs.decision.perceptual-quality-contract

### Revision 1 — A minimum SSIMULACRA2 score is the public lossy contract; Fast (70) and Balanced (85) are the production efforts; Quality stays feature-gated until it is smaller at matched score

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.decision.perceptual-quality-contract/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-cli/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-perceptual/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-plan-render/**"`, `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl/**"`, `path "JPXL/tools/**"`

Normal lossy encoding is specified by a minimum perceptual score, not a byte budget: the encoder minimises exact codestream bytes subject to SSIMULACRA2(source, decoded) >= requested score. Two production efforts exist: Fast (web; default --quality 70) and Balanced (archival; default --quality 85). Both accept an explicit --quality 0..100; 100 routes to lossless; the same score must mean the same minimum quality at every effort, and higher effort may only reduce bytes or overshoot, never the achieved score. Hard probe/price budgets are enforced in code for both production efforts with no hidden exhaustive fallback. The exhaustive RateSearchPreset::Quality path and the perceptual Quality effort (policy bank, terminal reducer) are compiled only under the `quality-effort` cargo feature; a public Quality effort is re-exposed only when evidence on the locked holdout shows geomean bytes at matched achieved SSIMULACRA2 <= 0.98x Balanced with Contract B guards intact. --bpp, --bytes and a fixed-quantizer --global-scale remain as expert, benchmarking and constrained-delivery modes; they no longer define the normal lossy policy. Quality-mode policy contains no requested-bitrate branch (at_most_one_bpp and the bpp-keyed chroma QM arms are removed from the quality path); chroma allocation is a per-preset starting value and a policy-bank axis compared at equal score. The production metric is the in-tree jpxl-perceptual implementation (first backend: clean-room SSIMULACRA2, parity-tested); a metric-version change is an encoder-behaviour change.

**Context.** The byte-target contract made the lossy path unusable for real work: a user cannot ask for archival or web quality, only for a byte count whose perceptual meaning changes per image (user, 2026-08-22). The G0 baseline of 2026-08-21 already shows JPXL Balanced 9-12% smaller than cjxl -e7 at equal SSIMULACRA2 on the mid/large photos while trailing Butteraugli 3-norm and PSNR at matched bytes, so the goal is a usable score contract that preserves that byte advantage and the guard metrics, not a libjxl density chase. The registered 2026-08-21 controller plan and the 2026-08-22 metric advice are the outside sources; this decision adopts the controller plan's public contract and effort semantics, keeps the doc's PR 1-5 and PR 7 in scope with PR 6/8 as follow-ups, and records the metric advice as a separate later workstream (JPXL-PQ/JPXL-PCost) in which SSIMULACRA2 and Butteraugli remain independent guards.

**Consequences.** Supersedes jpegxl-rs.decision.lossy-production-presets/1 (Quality as a public exhaustive reference preset). Work is tracked under jpegxl-rs.track.perceptual-quality-controller as PR 0-5 and PR 7 work records with measurable gates; promotion is measured at equal achieved SSIMULACRA2 (geomean byte ratio, BD-rate), never at equal bpp. Rate-mode (--bpp/--bytes) production streams must remain byte-identical through the refactors. The wall-time budget for the perceptual Balanced path is recorded per PR from measurement (provisional PR 4 bound 2.0x rate-mode Balanced at matched score; +25% is the later profiling target), not assumed.

**supersedes** `@jpegxl-rs.decision.lossy-production-presets/1`

## jpegxl-rs.decision.rate-ladder-interleaves-hfmul-above-the-ceiling

### Revision 1 — Above the global_scale ceiling the rate ladder interleaves HfMul with global_scale and couples quant_lf up to 16

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.decision.rate-ladder-interleaves-hfmul-above-the-ceiling/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/src/rate.rs"` · topic `rate-ladder-upper-segments`

Rungs above MAX_GLOBAL_SCALE are no longer whole HfMul multiples at the ceiling. Segment k (k = 2..=65) walks global_scale from floor((k-1)*MAX/k)+1 up to MAX with HfMul = k, so consecutive rungs differ by k units of effective scale (global_scale * HfMul) and segments join within k+1 units; the ladder top stays 65 * MAX. QuantizerChoice::at couples quant_lf to the segment as the largest base * j (j <= k) that stays at or below 16, so the LF/HF balance the ladder holds below the ceiling carries through the first segments; beyond that bound quant_lf stays put. Search paths that recover a quant_lf from a QuantizerChoice must carry the request's base value, never the coupled wire value.

**Context.** Phase Q3's first standing measurement showed the frame-constant HfMul rungs were a rate cliff: HfMul 2 at the ceiling is a full octave finer than HfMul 1, a 65% byte jump on the smooth mid2 photo, so every target between them landed 35% under ('budget spent, not at the ladder's limit'), and large at 2 bpp landed 27% under. The coupling bound of 16 is the product MAX_GLOBAL_SCALE * 16 that the fixed-quantizer defaults have always been allowed to reach; jxl-oxide 0.12.6 narrows LfQuant samples to signed 16 bits (Phase 5F) and a synthetic high-contrast oracle fixture wraps at twice that product.

**Consequences.** Cells whose crossing lies above the ceiling now reach their targets (mid2 2 bpp 698 KB -> 1,080 KB, +2.84 SSIMULACRA2, -31% Butteraugli; large 2 bpp 2.18 MB -> 3.0 MB, +1.6..+2.1 SSIMULACRA2, -18..-22% Butteraugli); every cell below the ceiling keeps its Phase Q2 hash. Balanced still falls back to the exhaustive controller on such cells because the second-anchor guess extrapolates with exponent 2 (about 5.9 s on mid2 at 2 bpp) — a speed follow-up, recorded separately. Requests with quant_lf already at or above 16 see an LF-step sawtooth of at most 1/(k+1) across segment joins above the ceiling.

## jpegxl-rs.decision.read-u32-wraps

### Revision 1 — read_u32 wraps mod 2^32, it does not error

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.decision.read-u32-wraps/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-bitstream/**"` · topic `read-u32-overflow`

Per 18181-1 B.2.2, read_u32 computes (offset + v) Umod (1 << 32): it wraps with
wrapping_add and never returns Overflow on offset + payload. Regression test
u32_offset_plus_payload_wraps_mod_2_pow_32. Do not harden this back into an error.

**Context.** Recovered from HANDOFF "Already fixed" (2026-08-02). The original scaffold returned Overflow; the fix carries a clause citation.

## jpegxl-rs.decision.retire-performance-md

### Revision 1 — Retire PERFORMANCE.md as plan-of-record for performance

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.decision.retire-performance-md/1` · scope `path ".agent/scratch/**"`, `path "JPXL/docs/**"` · topic `performance-docs-authority`

JPXL/docs/PERFORMANCE.md is no longer the plan-of-record for performance
baselines, measurement rules, or profiling results. Authority is split:

- Durable claims (baseline rules, bench entry points, summary observations,
  decisions): AKR records under jpegxl-rs.policy.performance-baseline-rules,
  jpegxl-rs.policy.jpxl-bench-entry-points, and jpegxl-rs.observation.preopt-*
  (and successors).
- Full raw run logs, flamegraph artifacts, HOTSPOTS/PROVENANCE: .agent/scratch/
  (not pruned by akr build). Current ladder:
  .agent/scratch/preopt-baseline-2026-08-06.md; current flamegraphs:
  .agent/scratch/flamegraphs/preopt-2026-08-06/.

PERFORMANCE.md remains only as a short stub pointing at those AKR keys and
scratch paths. Do not re-accumulate tables or rules in the markdown file.
Frozen experiment writeups may still go in JPXL/docs/experiments/ when an
experiment report is warranted.

**Context.** PERFORMANCE.md duplicated material that already lived as AKR observations and was drifting from scratch logs. AGENTS.md living-docs discipline prefers small generated views over hand-maintained performance tables.

**Consequences.** Opt-F acceptance and work language that required PERFORMANCE.md baseline rows must be revised to AKR observations + baseline-rules policy. Agents update observations and scratch, not long tables in PERFORMANCE.md.

## jpegxl-rs.decision.ssimulacra2-is-the-primary-promotion-metric

### Revision 1 — Optimize for SSIMULACRA2 first; butteraugli becomes a secondary axis to refine later

`active` · `@jpegxl-rs.decision.ssimulacra2-is-the-primary-promotion-metric/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-encode-policy/**"`, `path "test-set/**"`

SSIMULACRA2 is the primary metric for promoting a lossy encoder policy. Butteraugli is retained as a reported secondary axis and as the eventual refinement target, but it no longer holds a veto.

Concretely, replacing the previously implicit Contract B tie-break ('uniformly non-regressing Butteraugli without material SSIMULACRA2 loss'):

- A candidate is promotable when SSIMULACRA2 does not regress materially on any screened cell and improves on the corpus as a whole. Butteraugli is reported per cell and pooled, and a butteraugli regression is a recorded caveat rather than a blocker.
- Both metrics are still measured and both still appear in every screen table. This changes which one decides, not what is collected.
- The rule is stated BEFORE each screen runs, per the process note Phase 7.0 raised.

**Context.** Phase 7.0 demonstrated that a single lever can move the two metrics in opposite directions reliably and at scale: a rate-aware quantizer improved butteraugli in 20 of 28 cells (mean -5.21%, best -29.9%) while regressing SSIMULACRA2 in 24 of 28 (mean -1.80), at properly matched rate. With no stated tie-break, the promotion decision would have been made by whichever metric happened to be quoted first. The two metrics are not interchangeable. Butteraugli aggregates by max-norm and rewards reduced peak error, so it favours smoothing; SSIMULACRA2 is structure- and detail-sensitive and penalises lost texture. Phase 7.0's over-zeroing is exactly that divergence. User decision, 2026-08-12: optimize for SSIMULACRA2 and refine for perceptual later.

**Consequences.** IMMEDIATE. Phase 6.5's quantizer-donated frequency weight becomes promotable and is promoted. It was rejected under the old rule solely because butteraugli was not uniformly non-regressing. Re-read with SSIMULACRA2 primary it improves 14 of 14 scenes at 0.5 and 1 bpp (mean +4.85 and +0.70), is neutral at 2 and 4 bpp (mean -0.00 and -0.07, worst single cell -0.18), and butteraugli is ALSO net positive pooled (better in 17 of 28, mean -0.17%) -- so it is not even a trade. Phase 7.0's rate-distortion quantizer stays rejected, now for the primary reason rather than a secondary one. HISTORICAL PROMOTIONS REMAIN VALID, with one caveat to revisit. Phase 5G (AQ Off, quant_lf 8, no LF fill) was promoted on butteraugli but also improved SSIMULACRA2 in 10 of its 12 cells; the exceptions are small3/1 (-0.37) and small4/1 (-4.37). That small4/1 loss is material under the new rule and should be re-examined when the corpus next gets attention -- it is recorded here rather than silently inherited. Phase 5I (active EPF, uniform Sharpness 7) improved SSIMULACRA2 in 11 of 12 cells with a single -0.0351 exception and is unaffected. WHAT THIS DOES NOT MEAN. Butteraugli is not abandoned. The measured corpus gap against cjxl effort-7 is still stated in butteraugli terms, and closing it remains the track's goal; this decision orders the work, putting a metric the encoder can currently move in a consistent direction first. When the track returns to butteraugli it will do so with the structural deficits (rate proxy, quantizer) already addressed, which is the condition Phase 7.0 showed was missing.

## jpegxl-rs.decision.xyb-inverse-matrix-normative

`proposed` · `@jpegxl-rs.decision.xyb-inverse-matrix-normative/1` · scope `path "JPXL/crates/jpxl-core/**"` · topic `xyb-inverse-matrix`

OPSIN_ABSORBANCE_INVERSE_MATRIX matches 18181-1 L.2.1 Table L.1 defaults
digit-for-digit at f32; it is normative, not provisional. The spec signals
opsin_bias0..2 as negative (decoder side); the forward-side positive bias is the
same convention mirrored, documented in jpxl-core/src/color.rs.

## jpegxl-rs.policy.sources-advice-completion

### Retain external advice under sources/; mark completion in AKR

`superseded` · `@jpegxl-rs.policy.sources-advice-completion/1` · scope `all` · topic `sources-advice`

External architecture and optimization advice documents are retained under
the repository sources/ tree (for example sources/outside-advice.md) and
must not be deleted solely because their recommendations were adopted.
Progress against such a document is recorded only through AKR: propose or
revise work and milestones for each phase, attach evidence, and complete
those records when acceptance checks pass. Do not rewrite the advice
document into a checklist of strikethroughs or a second plan-of-record;
cite its path from AKR records instead.
